title: AWS Marketplace SaaS listing review notes — Redwood Inference (Hosted API + Dedicated/Private via private offer)
source_context: Working doc compiled from 2026-01-14 AWS Marketplace listing review sync (AWS: Megan Li, Andrew Patel, Sara Kline) plus follow-up guidance received asynchronously from Andrew on 2026-01-16 (updated checklist/screenshots) and internal edits through 2026-02-01.
summary:
AWS Marketplace team walked Redwood through SaaS listing requirements and common rejection reasons. Focus was on security documentation expectations (SOC 2/ISO posture wording, data handling, encryption/KMS, audit logs, retention) and how to present shared responsibility in the listing + attachments. AWS recommended tightening claims (avoid absolute compliance statements), ensuring support and refund language is explicit, and providing a clean architecture/data flow diagram.

UPDATED since the call: Andrew noted current review queues are running longer than the earlier estimate; plan for ~7–12 business days for first-pass review when the submission is complete, with security clarification cycles adding ~1–3 days per round. Redwood moved target submission from 2026-01-29 to 2026-02-03 to include final screenshots + revised security packet and to avoid a rushed first pass.
topics: SaaS offer listing fields and required links/attachments
Security review expectations (data handling clarity, encryption specificity, claims discipline)
Acceptable vs risky compliance language (SOC 2/ISO, HIPAA, GDPR, regulated workloads)
Data flow diagram + shared responsibility table guidance
Support SLAs, contact monitoring, and refund policy clarity
Metering dimension naming and billing stability
Submission timeline, review iterations, and gating of evidence
notes:
Attendees (Redwood): Jordan Blake (owner), Soojin Lee (PMM), Chris Osei (product ops), Naomi Feldman (security/compliance), Cole Summers (billing/metering), Alex Martinez (docs/devex)
Attendees (AWS): Megan Li (Partner SA), Andrew Patel (Vendor Program), Sara Kline (Security reviewer)

What AWS consistently flags:
1) Ambiguous data handling
- Where prompts/inputs/outputs go
- Whether anything is stored by default
- Default retention duration and how customers modify it
- Whether prompts are included in “logs” by default; define “telemetry” vs “application logs” vs “content/prompt logs”

2) Encryption statements that are too vague
- Avoid “we encrypt everything” with no specifics
- Prefer explicit: TLS version for in-transit + encryption at rest + key mgmt model (AWS KMS, CMK/BYOK if applicable)

3) Over-claims / implied endorsements
- Avoid “AWS approved” / “AWS endorsed” phrasing
- Avoid unconditional compliance claims (HIPAA/FedRAMP/PCI) unless fully supportable and scoped

Language guidance captured verbatim-ish:
- SOC 2: do NOT say “SOC 2 certified.” SOC 2 is an attestation. Preferred: “SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA/upon request” (and describe request process).
- ISO: “ISO 27001 certified” is only OK if scope clearly covers the service; otherwise use “aligned with ISO 27001 controls” and stay precise.
- HIPAA: do NOT claim “HIPAA compliant” in the listing. If true, conditional language is acceptable (e.g., “BAA available for eligible customers via private offer” / “supports HIPAA-eligible architectures”) but route through sales/legal.

Marketplace listing content expectations (minimum viable clarity):
- “How it works” must be explicit: subscribe in AWS → entitlement created → redirect to Redwood to create/link org → entitlement check → API key / onboarding → first call.
- Include entitlement propagation troubleshooting: avoid a hard promise (“10–15 minutes”) and instead say “may take several minutes” + what error looks like + escalation path.
- Screenshots: 3–6, readable when scaled; do not include customer names/sensitive data.

Procurement path clarity:
- Public offer = Hosted usage-based.
- Dedicated/Private deployments are via private offer/contract path; public listing may describe them but must not imply “click-buy instant provisioning” if fulfillment is not instant.

Metering dimensions:
- Dimension names show up on invoices; keep customer-friendly and stable.
- Recommendation: keep simple (“Text tokens”, “Embedding units”) and link to docs for exact mapping.

Data residency/residency wording:
- If we mention “EU region” / “data residency” we must specify what it covers: request processing, log storage, support access, backups.
- Be explicit that Hosted is region-limited (today) and that Dedicated/Private offer additional region controls if true.

Security packet pattern AWS likes:
- A security overview PDF + attestation-style statements, with full audit report gated (NDA) rather than attached publicly.
- A simple table: data categories, location, retention, access.
- Architecture/data flow diagram with clear “what’s in AWS vs what’s in Redwood managed service.” Swimlanes are fine if not busy.
- Shared responsibility table: AWS vs Redwood vs Customer responsibilities.
- Subprocessors: provide a public page link; attachment can reference where to find it.

Copy edit example from Sara (flagged sentence):
- Avoid: “enterprise-grade security including encryption everywhere, full audit logs, and compliance for regulated workloads.”
- Prefer factual bullets: “TLS 1.2+ in transit”, “Encryption at rest using AWS KMS”, “Audit logs for admin/auth/key events exportable”, “Configurable retention controls” and “features to support regulated workloads” (with pointer to security overview).

Timeline (updated):
- Earlier verbal estimate in call: first pass ~5–10 business days.
- Follow-up from Andrew (2026-01-16): plan for ~7–12 business days first pass due to review queues, assuming complete artifacts.
- Security clarifications: each round typically adds ~1–3 days depending on vendor response time.

Open questions (still pending as of 2026-02-01):
- Whether gated links are acceptable for reviewer access: AWS prefers attachments or non-gated links; if gating is required, provide a reviewer-access method (alias or temporary access).
- Final screenshot sizing requirements: portal validates, but we should follow the latest checklist from Andrew and avoid old “1100px” guidance.

Internal decisions since the call:
- Target submission moved to 2026-02-03 (was 2026-01-29) to avoid avoidable review churn.
- Listing will clearly separate purchase paths: “Hosted API (pay-as-you-go) available via public offer; Dedicated/Private available via private offer.”
next_steps: Compile a single reviewer-ready security packet (PDF) including: security overview, shared responsibility table, data flow diagram, encryption/KMS details, audit log event categories, retention defaults + configuration knobs, and residency notes per deployment mode.
Update listing copy to remove or qualify absolute security/compliance claims; ensure SOC 2/ISO/HIPAA phrasing matches AWS guidance and our legal posture.

Confirm screenshots and “How it works” steps comply with current AWS Marketplace UX guidance for SaaS subscriptions; ensure screenshots are readable at Marketplace scale and scrubbed of sensitive data.
Finalize support contact info, support hours, and any tiered SLAs; avoid implying 24/7 support for self-serve Hosted if it is tier-gated.
Lock metering dimension display names to match billing catalog and documentation mapping; avoid late changes that would surface on invoices.
Submit draft listing in partner portal by 2026-02-03 and respond to clarification requests within 24 hours to minimize iteration latency.
